topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, outlines the scope of the cancer lecture series, and presents the key learning outcomes regarding environmental carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Factors, Heredity, and Environmental Exposures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and explore the interplay between intrinsic cellular errors, inherited genetic risk, and environmental exposures reflected in global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on biological carcinogens, detailing how viral, bacterial, and parasitic infections drive oncogenesis with a detailed case study of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how physical agents and chemical carcinogens—including aflatoxins, UV light, polycyclic hydrocarbons, dioxins, and aromatic amines—cause DNA damage directly or through xenobiotic metabolism.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Context
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic mechanisms in carcinogenesis, emphasizing the multi-stage initiator-promoter paradigm, inflammation-driven growth, and developmental or tissue-specific susceptibilities.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the experimental, genomic, and population-level methods used to establish carcinogenicity, including mutational signature analysis, biobank epidemiology, animal bioassays, and the Ames test.
